Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-08-17 14:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Grace Liu (Redwood AE), Mateo Diaz (Redwood SE), Ivy Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Martens (CTO - PineGate), Raj Patel (Head of Ops), Sofia Nguyen (Security Architect), Tom Keller (Infra Lead)
Link: Redwood private deployment runbook (placeholder)

--- Auto-generated Summary (may contain errors):
PineGate wants an on-prem, no-egress deployment in their GMP facility. Main concerns: how are updates applied without internet, who signs the update, how to prove chain-of-custody for patches, and hardware constraints in their validated racks.

--- Transcript Body:
[00:00] Grace: Alright everybody thanks for coming, I'm Grace from Redwood, with Mateo and Ivy, we'll run through how we can do private/on-prem deployments for regulated labs. How's the time, Elena?
[00:08] Elena: Good, thanks. We've had a few seats of the intro but this is really, you know, the detailed intake. We operate inside GMP environment, no outbound internet from inference nodes, and updates must go through our SOP and a three-person signature.
[00:22] Grace: Got it. So no egress, break-glass exceptions only, and a multi-signer approval for updates. That's common. Mateo, maybe walk through the high level options?
[00:31] Mateo: Sure. There are three paths folks choose: hosted (not applicable here), Redwood Dedicated in a customer-vpc with limited egress — again usually blocking for you — and Redwood Private which can be air-gapped. For Private we support signed update bundles, a verification step on the appliance that checks signatures, and optional HSM attestations.
[00:50] Raj: Quick clarifying q, when you say signed bundle, do you mean we need to carry USB sticks physically to the data center? Or can we do some networked es- I mean we can't do networked egress.
[01:00] Mateo: Both patterns exist. For fully air-gapped you do a physical media handoff — we call it an airlock handoff. The bundle is signed by Redwood's signing key and optionally re-signed by your internal KMS in a staging machine before being imported. For semi-airgapped there's a secure staging machine that can fetch via a controlled proxy.
[01:18] Sofia: We need chain-of-custody evidence for every update — timestamps, who signed off, what package hashes — and log continuity for audits. Can your agents produce immutable audit logs we can ship to our central SIEM?
[01:30] Ivy: Yes, we can emit audit logs locally and forward them to your internal SIEM during the staging window. We also support signing metadata that includes approver IDs and can store that in the local audit store. Note that for true air-gapped you export logs manually or via a secure courier.
[01:47] Elena: And what about key management? We require HSM-backed keys for signing production images. No software-only KMS.
[01:54] Mateo: We integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS#11 on the staging host, or we can use a customer HSM on-prem that holds the signing key. Redwood's system supports verifying signatures against cert chains where the root is your HSM.
[02:07] Tom: On hardware — our racks are compact. We currently run a mix of 2x A40 and 1x A100 per rack, but there's limited U space. What's the minimal footprint for a single model serving node if we want low-latency predictions?
[02:19] Mateo: It depends on model size and batch. For a 7B model optimized and quantized, you can do inference on a single A40 with careful kernel selection; larger LLMs require A100s or multiple GPUs with KV cache sharding. Also consider latency SLOs — continuous batching helps cost but adds tail latency.
[02:36] Raj: Our success criteria are: zero unplanned egress; validated update workflow with audit trail; under 50ms p95 for internal inference calls; and predictable monthly unit cost.
[02:48] Grace: Great, that's helpful. For the p95 budget we can propose a Dedicated pool in your private network vs a Private air-gapped instance and show cost deltas.
[02:57] [00:03:00] Elena: One more on rollback. Say a patch causes a regression in output quality—what's your rollback story when you're offline?
[03:08] Mateo: We support signed rollout manifests that include both the current and previous image hashes. The appliance keeps a verified snapshot of the previous image for fast rollback. Rollback still requires an approval event in your SOP, though we can script an emergency rollback that toggles to the previous hash if you allow pre-authorized fallbacks.
[03:29] Sofia: We're strict about runtime attestation — we want to prove that the binary running at any time matches the signed artifact. Do you have runtime attestation?
[03:37] Ivy: We have a lightweight attestor that validates binary hashes at boot and periodically verifies KV cache integrity. For higher assurance, we can integrate with TPM or HSM-based attestation flows, but that will require some infra work on your side.
[03:50] Raj: How do you handle dependency updates — like kernel patches — if we can't reboot racks often due to validation windows?
[03:58] Mateo: We can bundle OS and runtime patches into a maintenance window and provide a dry-run mode in a staging environment. Also support rolling windows across racks so you don't take everything down at once.
[04:12] [00:04:12] Elena: Policy stuff — we have to record who approved each step. Can the approval workflow be configured so the system refuses to accept unsigned images, and logs the approver IDs?
[04:23] Grace: Yes. The import step validates signatures and reads an approval manifest. If manifest is missing or insufficient signers, import fails. That validation is in the appliance and enforced before any image is unpacked.
[04:33] Tom: Any limits on bundle size? We have models that are 60GB after quantization.
[04:38] Ivy: No hard limit, but large bundles take longer to transfer via physical media. We recommend delta updates for weight patches and use KV cache priming to reduce startup time. Also can provide checksumed chunking to resume transfer if a media fails.
[04:52] Sofia: For audits we need immutable logs with sequence numbers. We also have to show retention and rotation. Do you provide configurable retention policies?
[05:00] Mateo: Yes, retention is configurable locally. We also support export to your archive system during approved windows. For non-networked setups you can export via signed tarballs and import to your long-term archive.
[05:11] [00:05:11] Raj: Who from Redwood will be on-call during the pilot? We need named contacts and escalation paths for the POC window.
[05:18] Grace: I'll be primary AE contact, Mateo will be SE lead, Ivy is backup for update engineering. We'll share a contact card and SLA for the pilot after this call.
[05:27] Elena: Timeline — we're aiming to kick off a POC in two weeks, run for three weeks, and then bring in QA for validation.
[05:35] Grace: That matches our usual process. We'll send a POC checklist and a hardware requirements matrix.
[05:40] [00:05:40] Sofia: One more: do you support SSO for the console and RBAC mapping to our LDAP? We don't want vendor accounts floating around.
[05:49] Mateo: Yes, we support SAML/SSO and can map roles. For private deployments, the control plane can be run inside your VPC or a customer-controlled plane, and accounts can be federated to your IdP.
[05:59] Raj: Any gotchas for validation or regulatory evidence?
[06:02] Ivy: The usual is to include SBOM for the runtime and a chain-of-custody for updates. We can help generate a package manifest per build that lists versions, hashes, and build provenance.
[06:14] [00:06:14] Elena: Pricing touch — high level, will you send ranges for a private on-prem plus support? We must budget for 3 months of pilot and then an annual support fee.
[06:21] Grace: Yes we'll include ballpark numbers — license + support + optional on-site engineering for the pilot.
[06:26] Sofia: Competitors — we've looked at RivalAI's airgapped offering but they didn't have a clean HSM integration and their audit logs were messy. BigCloudAI had a lot of enterprise features but required a hybrid egress pattern which we can't accept.
[06:38] Mateo: Good to know. Redwood focuses on clear offline patterns and HSM integration for these regulated customers.
[06:44] [00:06:44] Elena: Any concerns about model upgrades? Our models are internally developed and updated often — we need a process to push new weights multiple times per month.
[06:54] Mateo: We recommend a signed staging pipeline: developer uploads -> staging build machine (in allowed network) -> sign with your HSM -> deliver via airlock. For frequent updates we'll suggest incremental weight diffs and prewarming to reduce cold start.
[07:08] Raj: Ok last thing — emergency patches. If a critical vuln hit, how fast can we get a hotfix imported given your process?
[07:16] Ivy: With pre-authorized emergency fallback, and if you allow a 'break-glass' token with recorded justification, we can get a hotfix applied within a validated window within hours. Otherwise, we follow your multi-signer SLA which may add days.
[07:29] [00:07:29] Grace: Let's do a quick recap and next steps. We'll send the private deployment runbook, an example signed bundle workflow, a hardware matrix template, and ballpark pricing. Mateo will prepare a short demo/offline update video. PineGate to send patch window and approval policy.
[07:46] Elena: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[07:48] Raj: Thanks.
[07:49] Sofia: Thanks, bye.
